catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Analysis focused on agentic architecture: orchestration, governance, LLM abstraction, state persistence, and knowledge management. Primary evidence from src/cas_runner, cas-knowledge structure, and architecture docs.
analysis_limits: Only key source files were provided; full contents of runner.py and governance modules were not fully inspected.
Documentation (docs/architecture/*) may be aspirational, not reflecting implemented behaviour.
No runtime execution or test results were available.

system_map.overview: cas_runner is an agentic orchestrator for Continuous Architecture Stewardship: it initialises workspaces, runs multi-step flows (FlowRunner) that invoke LLM-backed steps, validates outputs via compliance and governance action engines, and persists evidence and knowledge in cas-knowledge directories.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Sequential orchestrator: executes steps with a shared mutable context

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: State transition authority: validates and executes governance actions against a transition registry

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Guardrail: checks agent outputs against compliance rules

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Knowledge writer: merges AI-generated governance blocks into existing documents

agents.name: LiteLLMClient / MockLLMClient
agents.role: LLM tool provider: isolates agent execution from model backend

orchestration.description: FlowRunner drives all steps sequentially; governance and compliance engines act as validation gates before/after step execution.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLM
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provide a unified interface to multiple LLM providers

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Enable deterministic testing without external LLM calls

tools_and_integrations.name: Git deltas
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provide evidence for architectural steering decisions

state_and_memory.description: cas-knowledge directories store decisions, rules, patterns, and project-specific knowledge as markdown/JSON files.
FlowRunner context object carries step-to-step state within a run.
SteeringRuntimeIndex derives capability records and architectural deltas from git changes and prompt facts.
Runtime evaluation results and traces are stored for audit and learning.

patterns.name: Provider Abstraction for Deterministic Agent Execution

tool_protocols.notes: LLM calls are made through a standard client interface, not via MCP or explicit tool calling.

optimisation_targets.notes: Abstraction enables swap between real and mock providers, improving test reliability and portability.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Using a thin client interface keeps agent code simple and deterministic.

patterns.summary: LLM access is isolated behind a client interface so agent steps can run against real or mock providers.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent execution from LLM backend to enable testing and portability.
patterns.context: Used by the CAS runner for all LLM-backed agent steps.
forces: Need to test agent flows without external LLM costs
Support provider switching to avoid vendor lock-in
Keep agent code independent of SDK specifics
patterns.solution: Define LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient implementing the same interface; agent code depends on the interface, not on a concrete provider.
implementation_signals: Two client classes with similar method signatures
Agent steps accept a client instance

benefits: Provider switching without agent code changes
failure_modes: If clients diverge, tests may pass with mock but fail with real provider

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt whenever agent code calls LLM directly; create a mock client for deterministic testing.

patterns.name: Sequential Flow Pipeline with Shared Context

tool_protocols.notes: Steps are executed by the orchestrator; no dynamic tool invocation.

optimisation_targets.notes: Sequential execution makes flows predictable and easier to debug.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: A fixed step sequence limits autonomy but improves reproducibility.

patterns.summary: FlowRunner executes a deterministic sequence of steps, passing a mutable context object.
patterns.intent: Enable stepwise agent execution with predictable ordering and shared state.
patterns.context: Core execution model for the CAS runner, as described in architecture docs.
forces: Need reproducible flow execution
Steps may need to share state
Must allow adding/removing steps without breaking orchestration
patterns.solution: Runner iterates over a list of steps, each receives and mutates a common context object; errors can be handled centrally.

costs: Limited flexibility for dynamic step selection
Steps may become tightly coupled via context
failure_modes: Context mutation can cause hidden dependencies between steps

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a sequential pipeline when agent tasks have a fixed, known execution order and shared context is acceptable.

patterns.name: Transition-Governed Action State Machine

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions are validated through code, not tool calls.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enforces that governance actions only follow allowed transitions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows autonomy within defined state boundaries.

patterns.summary: Governance actions are only allowed when a registered transition from current state to next state exists.
patterns.intent: Ensure governance workflows only move through approved states, preventing invalid actions.
patterns.context: Used by the governance engine to manage lifecycle transitions in the CAS system.
forces: Need explicit control over state changes
Agents should not skip governance steps
Must be auditable
patterns.solution: TransitionRegistry holds valid from/to pairs; GovernanceActionEngine refuses actions that are not registered.

benefits: Prevents accidental or malicious invalid transitions
costs: Requires maintaining registry as new states appear
failure_modes: If registry is incomplete, valid transitions may be blocked

patterns.reuse_notes: Use an explicit transition registry whenever workflow state changes must be strictly controlled.

patterns.name: Compliance Engine as Output Guardrail

tool_protocols.notes: Validation is code-driven using rule context.

optimisation_targets.notes: Reduces risk of agent outputs violating rules.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents are free to produce outputs, but a gate checks them.

patterns.summary: Agent-produced outputs are checked against compliance rules before being accepted.
patterns.intent: Prevent non-compliant decisions from entering the knowledge base or governance state.
patterns.context: Applied after agent steps that generate architecture decisions or other knowledge artifacts.
forces: Need to enforce organisational rules
Agents may generate plausible but non-compliant content
patterns.solution: ComplianceEngine loads rule context (e.g., from rule-context.json) and evaluates agent output against those rules.

costs: May reject outputs that are valid but not covered by rules
failure_modes: If rule-context is incomplete, agent can slip through

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt a post-processing compliance check whenever agent outputs must adhere to external rules.

patterns.name: Merge-Based Agentic Document Update

tool_protocols.notes: Agent output is merged into existing markdown files.

optimisation_targets.notes: Preserves existing content while integrating new agent-generated information.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Autonomy is limited by the merge process, which keeps human-edited content intact.

patterns.summary: AI-generated content is merged into existing knowledge documents rather than replacing them.
patterns.intent: Allow agents to update shared knowledge without overwriting prior decisions or human edits.
patterns.context: Used for governance block updates and knowledge document evolution.
forces: Knowledge base is persistent and shared
Agent output should not clobber existing context
Need traceability of agent changes
patterns.solution: AgenticMerger takes generated content and merges it into the target file using merge rules that preserve existing structure.
implementation_signals: Merge logic invoked on governance block update

costs: Merge may introduce conflicts or require careful design
failure_modes: If merge rules are too permissive, agent content may overwrite important context

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a dedicated merger component when agents must update persistent documents in a collaborative manner.

patterns.name: Evidence-First Steering Index

tool_protocols.notes: Data is derived from git deltas and prompt facts, not from agent memory.

optimisation_targets.notes: Grounds steering decisions in observable facts.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents use the index as a source of truth, reducing hallucination risk.

patterns.summary: Steering state is derived from git deltas and prompt facts, not from assumptions or stale memory.
patterns.intent: Base architectural steering decisions on current, verifiable data.
patterns.context: Used to construct the steering runtime index and capability lineage.
forces: Need to avoid stale or hallucinated context
Git history is a reliable source of change evidence
patterns.solution: Models like RawGitDelta and ArchitecturalDelta are populated from git changes, then used to build SteeringRuntimeIndex.

failure_modes: If git deltas are incomplete, index may be misleading

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt an evidence-first approach whenever agent state must reflect reality.

patterns.name: Structured Prompt Facts

tool_protocols.notes: Prompt inputs are typed Pydantic models.

optimisation_targets.notes: Typed prompt facts reduce ambiguity and validation errors.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Fixed schema constrains prompt content to ensure predictability.

patterns.summary: Agent prompts are assembled from typed PromptFact objects to enforce contract.
patterns.intent: Provide consistent, validated inputs to LLM calls, reducing ambiguity.
patterns.context: Appears in steering models, likely used to prepare context for LLM calls.
forces: LLM prompts often contain unstructured free text
Need to pass specific facts reliably
patterns.solution: Define a Pydantic model (PromptFact) with typed fields; agents construct facts before sending to LLM.

benefits: Clear contract between agent and model
costs: May require casting arbitrary data to schema
failure_modes: If schema becomes too rigid, it may reject useful information

patterns.reuse_notes: Use structured prompt facts to reduce hallucination and improve testability of prompt construction.

patterns.name: Reproducible Workspace Bootstrap

tool_protocols.notes: Bootstrap prepares filesystem and governance block before agent runs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures every agent run starts from a known, clean state.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automated bootstrap reduces manual setup and configuration drift.

patterns.summary: Agent environments are initialized via bootstrap that sets up directories and merges the governance block.
patterns.intent: Provide a consistent starting context for agent workflows.
patterns.context: Entry point for the CAS runner; ensures required files and governance configuration exist.
forces: Agent workflows depend on workspace structure
Governance configuration must be present
patterns.solution: Bootstrap function initialises workspace directories, creates default files, and merges CAS governance block into existing files.

costs: Bootstrap logic can become complex if workspace evolves
failure_modes: If bootstrap is skipped, agents may fail or produce inconsistent state

patterns.reuse_notes: Create a dedicated bootstrap step for any agentic system that depends on a structured workspace.

patterns.name: Template-Forced Knowledge Artifacts

tool_protocols.notes: Shared template files act as a contract for all agent-generated knowledge.

optimisation_targets.notes: Standardised artifacts are easier to parse and validate.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Templates constrain agent output to a fixed structure, limiting improvisation.

patterns.summary: Knowledge artifacts (ADRs, patterns, signals) follow markdown templates that enforce structure.
patterns.intent: Ensure all agent-generated knowledge artifacts have a consistent, parseable structure.
patterns.context: The cas-knowledge/templates directory contains templates for decisions, patterns, rules, signals, etc.
forces: Knowledge artifacts must be machine-readable
Agents may produce unstructured content
Need to support downstream validation and retrieval
patterns.solution: Define markdown templates with required sections; agents fill these templates when generating artifacts.

failure_modes: If templates are not enforced, agents may skip required fields

patterns.reuse_notes: Use markdown templates as contracts for any system where multiple agents (or humans) generate knowledge artifacts.

patterns.name: Runtime Evaluation and Trace Persistence

tool_protocols.notes: Execution traces are written to the filesystem for audit.

optimisation_targets.notes: Persistence allows post-hoc analysis and accountability.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents act freely but leave a trace.

patterns.summary: Execution traces and evaluations are stored in runtime directories for audit and learning.
patterns.intent: Enable auditability of agent runs and provide data for future learning.
patterns.context: The cas-knowledge/runtime directory includes traces and evaluations subdirectories.
forces: Need to understand why an agent made a decision
Should support continuous improvement
patterns.solution: Agent runner writes execution traces and evaluation results into designated directories.
implementation_signals: Presence of traces/ and evaluations/ directories

costs: Disk usage and potential sensitive data at rest
failure_modes: Traces may be lost if not integrated into the runner

patterns.reuse_notes: Persist trace data whenever agent actions need to be explainable or evaluated.

patterns.name: Externalized Rule Context

tool_protocols.notes: Governance rules are loaded from a JSON file, not hardcoded.

optimisation_targets.notes: Centralising rules reduces drift and makes updates safe.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents operate within rules that can be updated without code changes.

patterns.summary: Governance rules live in a JSON context file loaded at runtime, making agent behavior configurable.
patterns.intent: Separate governance rule definitions from agent logic.
patterns.context: ComplianceEngine and other governance components read rules from runtime context.
forces: Rules need to change faster than code
Different projects may have different governance requirements
patterns.solution: Store rules in a JSON file (rule-context.json) that is loaded at runtime and passed to validation engines.

benefits: Rules can be updated without deploying code
costs: Requires schema validation for rule file
failure_modes: If rule file is malformed, agent execution may fail

patterns.reuse_notes: Externalise rules and policies as data to make agent behaviour adaptable across environments.

patterns.name: Derived Health Monitoring

tool_protocols.notes: Health is computed from governance metrics, not agent self-report.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides a quick aggregate view of system health.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Health calculation is deterministic and transparent.

patterns.summary: System health is computed from governance metrics with reasons, giving agents a snapshot of overall state.
patterns.intent: Enable quick diagnosis of whether the governance system is operating normally.
patterns.context: Dashboard module computes health from governance metrics.
forces: Metrics are scattered across governance models
Need simple health summary for humans or agents
patterns.solution: HealthStatus enum and calculate_health function aggregate metrics, with get_health_reasons listing justifications.

costs: Health model may hide underlying complexity
failure_modes: If metrics are noisy, health may be inaccurate

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement a derived health model for any agentic system that needs a high-level operational status.

anti_patterns.name: Hardcoded Pipeline Values Inhibiting Agent Adaptation
symptoms: Installer versions pinned directly in workflow files
Validation script explicitly checks for zero hardcoding
impact: Agent-driven updates become difficult or impossible
Workflow drift between expected and actual state
suggested_remediation: Parameterize workflow via environment variables or config files

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Structured Pydantic models (PromptFact) and template-driven knowledge artifacts enforce consistent input/output formats.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Typed contracts reduce hallucination and improve parseability.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Health model, compliance engine, and runtime trace persistence provide multi-layered evaluation of agent outputs and system state.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Evaluation is both real-time (compliance) and post-hoc (traces, health).

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Transition registry and compliance guardrails restrict agent actions to allowed states and rule-conformant outputs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Safety is enforced via explicit state machines and external rule context.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Traces, evaluations, and health dashboard give operators and agents a view of system status and history.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Observability is file-based and simple, but may not scale to high-frequency runs.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: MockLLMClient allows deterministic tests without LLM spend, and LiteLLM abstraction enables switching to cheaper providers.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: No explicit cost tracking, but provider abstraction helps with cost management.
